mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate of more than 0.1% signals an easing monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns. The signal is always active (no threshold condition) and the direction is positive.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods with a 3-month FEDFUNDS decline > 0.1% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) is above 2.5%, it signals a monetary policy tightening cycle that increases real interest rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods where FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL > 2.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of low unemployment expansion (UNRATE < 5.0%), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns because a tight labor market supports corporate earnings growth through sustained consumer spending.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where UNRATE < 5.0% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts rate above 1800.0 thousand units signals strong demand for housing, which is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 returns because it indicates a robust economy and rising corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods where HOUST > 1800.0 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer credit (RSAFS) is above 320,000 million dollars and the federal funds rate is below 3.0%, it signals a strong consumer demand environment with accommodative monetary policy, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where RSAFS > 320000.0 and FEDFUNDS < 3.0% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising employment level (measured as the 3-month change in PAYEMS) is associated with positive 5-day S&P 500 returns because it signals a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth. The signal is always active (no threshold condition) and the direction is positive.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods where PAYEMS increased by more than 0.5% over the past 3 months are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns because it signals an economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods where INDPRO < 100.0 are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
